name: How do you choose between gas and induction in an ADU kitchen?

mainEntity.name: Which cooking option is better for a small ADU kitchen, gas or induction?
mainEntity.text: Which cooking option is better for a small ADU kitchen, gas or induction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choosing between gas and induction in an ADU kitchen usually comes down to utility access, cooking preferences, and how compact the space is. Induction is popular in small kitchens because it is fast, energy efficient, and easier to keep cool in tight quarters. It can also simplify some ventilation and comfort issues compared with gas. Gas cooking still has a loyal following because many cooks prefer the flame response and familiar control, but it may require more attention to venting and existing gas infrastructure. In Los Angeles-area ADUs, electrical capacity is often a deciding factor, especially if the project already includes HVAC, laundry, and other electric loads. The best decision should be made early because it affects panel sizing, appliance selection, countertop layout, and hood design. A good contractor can help compare the practical tradeoffs rather than just the brand preferences. For many compact ADUs, induction is the most flexible modern option.
